Debris from the plane was located on August 27, 1986 in Lake Erie, approximately 32 nautical miles south of the St.Thomas Airport. Debris was drifting in a southeast direction and was recovered approximately 1-3 nautical miles on the Canadian side of the international boundary line in Lake Erie. Debris was identified by Bud Field,  brother of Terry Field, as having come from the missing aircraft.

Case reference: 2014002458.CaseDesc: On September 4, 1986, Rozebeh Kiani was seen for the last time in the Shaughnessy Village district of Montreal, Quebec. Rozebeh left all his personal belongings behind in his apartment and it is possible he may have travelled to Vancouver, British Columbia. Case reference: 2014004911.CaseDesc: On July 3, 1974, Ellice Harper, his wife and their young child were out on the lake duck hunting and fishing on Red Sucker Lake, Manitoba. At one point in the day, the party stopped on shore to eat. During this stop, they noticed a storm coming in. By the time they left there were already waves forming as they started out across the lake. The wind increased and the waves were so strong that they would almost cause the vessel to flip over. The boat filled with water and a wave took him out of the boat. His wife and child drifted in the boat until they reached shore and were later rescued. It is presumed Ellice drowned.

Case reference: 2022054729.CaseDesc: Kenneth William Snedden was seen for the last time on October 28, 2022 at 1pm in McAdam, New Brunswick.  Kenneth was seen in his grey GMC Sierra with his ATV (red 2005 Honda TRX350F) in the truck bed to go hunting. His truck was found that same evening on Duck Lake Road in Prospect Ridge, New Brunswick, unattended and the ATV was no longer in the truck bed. On November 5th 2022, Kenneth's ATV was recovered in a marsh area of Dumfries Parish, New-Brunswick. Kenneth has not been heard from or seen since.
